content:
Parents are being urged to revisit the screen time limits they impose on their kids when they head back to school. It says stressed parents may take a more relaxed attitude to screen time during the summer break, and this can prove seriously detrimental to their children once the new school term begins.

Additionally, experts say that the two hours a day limit previously recommended is now outdated, and parents should take a more sophisticated approach based on “the 5 Cs” …

CNET notes that parents can be more stressed when kids are at home all day, and that can lead to greater reliance on electronic devices to keep them occupied.

Experts say this isn’t necessarily problematic.

But it can put your kids at risk unless changes are made once they return to school.

Child development experts say that too much media use can lead to lower academic achievement, attention control and cognition.

If you’re not sure how much screen time is appropriate for children of different ages, there is help on hand from the American Academy of Pediatrics:
